function.name: check_bpmn
function.description: Check BPMN 2.0 XML, from tok or from any modelling tool, with the BPMN rules of the tok checker, as `tok check FILE.bpmn --json`: every finding has a code, a severity, the line and the id of its element and a message. steps requires every element name to start with the step number of a process description (K01); description, the text of that description, reports steps without an element and elements without a step (K02, K03); camunda adds the Camunda 8 profile of executable models (C codes; with path, forms and decisions are looked for in the file's folder). XML with errors is a successful call with errors > 0. Codes are explained in the reference topic 'diagnostics'.

camunda.description: Also check the Camunda 8 profile of executable models (C codes).

description.description: The process description whose table lists the steps (its first column holds the step numbers); checks that every step is in the model (K02, K03).

path.description: Path of a .bpmn file, read by the server (relative to its working directory). Give either xml or path.

steps.description: Element names start with step numbers (K01).

xml.description: The BPMN 2.0 XML. Give either xml or path.

function.name: check_bpmn
function.description: Check BPMN 2.0 XML and list its diagnostics.

function.name: check
function.description: Check a tok document and list its diagnostics (code, severity, line, element, message), as `tok check --json`. Every layer is checked: tokens, statements, references, BPMN 2.0 rules, the Camunda 8 profile of executable documents, decisions, FEEL and simulation parameters. A document with errors is a successful call with errors > 0; fix the errors and check again. Codes are explained in the reference topic 'diagnostics'.

bpmn.description: Also check the BPMN 2.0 rules of the exported model (E, W, L codes).

class.description: BPMN 2.0.2 conformance class to check against; elements outside it are R075.

level.description: Teaching level: the elements the document may use (spec §13).

path.description: Path of a .tok file, read by the server (relative to its working directory). Give either text or path.

text.description: The tok document. Give either text or path.
